title: What exactly is so groundbreaking about Frozen?

commenti.body:
Not sure anyone considers it a masterpiece. It’s more than the Disney formula had grown kind of stale and the use of decidedly pop songs and a girl-led narrative that eschewed the typical “prince charming” made it stand out. 

That, and the fact that it’s really all a mataphor for menstrual flow.

I’m not sure who considers it a masterpiece? I think at the time it was praised for its songs and the fact that it’s ended subverted expectations in regards to the prince. I don’t think anyone has considered it high art, more so just enjoyable Disney fare.

I don't recall anyone claiming it was groundbreaking upon release. It's just a decent Disney Animated Feature. The songs are what it's best known for, and you can't deny its got some great catchy songs. 

You say the twist was predictable, but were you looking for a Sixth Sense or Seven twist? Its a kids movie, it has to be a twist they can follow along with. 

I would say a 7/10 is about exactly how it should be rated.

It is really the starting point of a paradigm shift within Disney and the narratives and type of films it releases. Pretty much every Disney film is some variation of: there's a princess who is locked away by an evil bad character and needs to be saved by some brave guy's true loves kiss. This was the formula Disney used when making it's animated films e.g. Tangled, Aladdin, Hercules, Beauty and The Beast. However when Disney purchased Pixar from Steve Jobs the types of stories that Pixar which is independent from Disney were quite different and one of the reasons for the success of Pixar comes from John Lassiter and the other writers in Pixar. So when Lassiter became the COO of Disney he would have an executive producing role in the Disney side of the animated films as well and it is here that you can see a growing change and with Frozen that the formula is completely altered. The "evil character" IS the princess and that it is not some true loves first kiss situation from a brave guy is not what saves her but it is actually the familial loving kiss from her sister that breaks the spell. This is the point in which Disney goes off of the old and tired and brings in a new age for Disney with fresh stories and the abandonment of old character archetypes that films such as big hero 6, Zootopia, Moana for example are made. And this is entirely because of Frozen.

Definately not groundbreaking but it was very popular for a reason I think. It’s a nicer Disney angle to have the movie be more about sisterhood than romance, and to have that classically Disney romance be a bait and switch.

My impression was that kids just loved it, particularly the music, so parents were just subjected to the Frozen lifestyle, and in time, they come to accept it and have to elevate the value in it in order to keep from going insane.  My theory is that the over the top reviews praising Frozen are written by people with children, who have been subjected to the film hundreds of time ([relevant article](https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/27/movies/frozen-2-repeat.html)). I think it's also why so many parents recommend that I (someone without kids) watch Bluey just because it's an amazing show for people of all ages. Is it an entertaining show for adults without kids? No, no way. Is it way better than tons of other shows that kids get hooked on, and with entertainment for parents thrown in? Yes, for sure. 

I also think a princess movie for children that focused more on the relationship between two sisters rather than a love story was seen as groundbreaking. And that Elsa is single, as far as I know. My nieces see themselves and their relationship in Frozen, and I think that's true for so many children who are sisters.

I think the novelty of making the chairlift the "villain" of the film is what has drawn people to it.  
People love practically shot one locations thrillers, especially in a "what would you do" sort of way, like we see here. There was a lot of fuss made over using real snow and making the actors physically cold for better performances.  
You could say it made for skiing what Jaws did for the ocean.
